title_en: Bruce Darringer, Founder BSD Strategic Advisors
title_zh: Bruce Darringer：BSD Strategic Advisors 创始人谈对冲基金的风险与运营
subtitle_zh: 以 Lehman 与新冠两次 VIX 破80事件为镜，剖析对冲基金投资风险之外的运营、资本与治理基础设施。
summary_zh: 本期 Alpha Exchange 中，主持人 Dean Curnutt 对话 BSD Strategic Advisors 创始人 Bruce Darringer（两人相识三十年）。Darringer 背景跨学科：本科海外学金融、Harvard Law 出身，做过公司并购（M&A）、高收益承销与衍生品（曾为 ISDA 制定标准化文件），后在量化对冲基金与 Goldman 并购辗转，2003 年加入信贷机构 King Street Capital Management 任首席运营官（COO），用 21 年把它从十几人、约 25 亿规模、专注困境投资的基金，做成超 250 人、逾 250 亿、覆盖几乎所有资产类别的多业务平台。本集以两次 VIX 突破 80 的事件——2008 年 11 月全球金融危机（GFC）中的 Lehman 与 2020 年 3 月新冠——为镜，剖析对冲基金投资风险之外的运营、资本与治理基础设施。他强调运营已从可与投资流程松耦合的独立实体，变为公司成功不可或缺的一环；面对小交易对手时主动谈好长期受用的 ISDA 条款、随时备有各对手条款矩阵以厘清敞口至关重要。他复盘新冠时若非 Zoom、Amazon 与云计算基础设施成熟，结果会截然不同；并谈到反身性（reflexivity）——投资者关系不牢时会“先赎回再问问题”、自我实现。节目还触及 AI 融入投顾流程，以及原子化/即时结算（atomic settlement）与 24/7 市场在消除延误风险的同时，给“需要睡觉的人”带来的新监控难题。是一堂关于对冲基金非投资风险与机构韧性的实务课。

turns.zh: 不只是对市场，还有对那些非常复杂的基础设施问题。做投资这行，要制造出回报本身就有挑战，但要把这类机构高效地运营起来，是非常复杂、非常繁难的。我想这也正是我特别期待向你请教的地方。先从你自己的职业生涯讲起吧。

turns.zh: 做的是公司业务和并购（M&A）的混合工作，还有一些高收益证券承销，以及一些衍生品相关的工作，既为企业客户提供建议，实际上也为 ISDA 本身提供建议，帮它制定标准化的文件。之后我在一家对冲基金初创公司——一家量化（quant）公司——待了几年，做完那段之后，

I joined King Street Capital Management, which is a large credit major joined when they were a dozen people, roughly two and a half billion under management. They had a distress focused hedge fund.
turns.zh: 我去了 Goldman 做并购执行，做了好几年。最终在2003年回到了对冲基金世界。我加入了 King Street Capital Management，这是一家大型信贷机构，我加入时他们只有十几个人，管理规模大约25亿。他们当时有一只专注困境投资的对冲基金。

turns.zh: 对我来说，加入他们担任首席运营官（COO）、真正把公司的基础设施搭建起来，是个很好的机会。我在那里度过了接下来的21年，真正帮助搭建公司运营端和投资端的方方面面。当我在2024年底离开公司时，

It had real estate business at a COO business, private credit business, and of course the traditional multi-stract credit

turns.zh: 有时来势还很猛。但投资风险远不只是屏幕上闪烁、制造出市场风险的价格。要搭建一家复杂的机构，里面牵扯的东西太多了，正如我前面提到的。所以在开始的时候，我想做的是找几个案例研究，好好向你请教，

turns.en: around all of the components of a hedge fund and how they need to react when the market finds itself inside a significant risk event. So we're going to use the two big ones. The two times the VIX went over 80. So we've got the GFC in November 2008 and then COVID March of 2020. Those are both VIX of 80 events.
turns.zh: 围绕对冲基金的各个组成部分，以及当市场陷入一场重大风险事件时，这些部分需要如何反应。所以我们要用两次最大的事件，也就是 VIX 两次超过80的时候。一次是2008年11月的全球金融危机（GFC），然后是2020年3月的新冠疫情。这两次都是 VIX 达到80的事件。

So perhaps starting with Lehman, of course, was a market-wide event, but it was a trading counterparty as well, a prime brokerage counterparty. I want you to just give us a sense as to what it means
turns.zh: 这些事件会给一家金融机构带来巨大的压力。这正是我想切入的地方。也许先从 Lehman 开始，它当然是一场波及整个市场的事件，但它同时也是一家交易对手、一家主经纪商（prime brokerage）对手。我想请你给我们讲讲，

turns.en: to manage through that, not just the investment risk, but all of the other aspects of the business that come under strain, under fire, during a time like that. Bring us back to that period and help us understand managing, again, not just investment risk, but all of the other aspects of the business that become stressed during that period.
turns.zh: 熬过那段时期意味着什么，不只是投资风险，还有业务中其他所有在那样时刻承受压力、遭受冲击的方面。带我们回到那段时期，帮我们理解如何管理，再说一次，不只是投资风险，还有业务中其他所有在那段时期变得紧张承压的方面。

turns.en: Yeah, Matt, say at a high level, it used to be 30 years ago, you could have the operations of these sorts of firms, the smaller hedge funds that existed at that time could be more of its own entity and maybe not as integrated with the investment process. Clearly, as the industry has grown, it really is fully integral to firm success.
turns.zh: 是的，我会说，从大的层面讲，30年前，这类公司的运营——当时存在的那些较小的对冲基金——可以更多地作为一个独立的实体，也许跟投资流程整合得没那么紧密。显然，随着这个行业壮大，运营已经真正完全成为公司成功不可或缺的一部分。

turns.en: As you said, these businesses are complicated, and if you don't have the right risk management infrastructure on the investment side, but also the risk management infrastructure on the operation side, which really covers and touches every part of the firm from human capital to investor capital, to technology, et cetera.
turns.zh: 正如你所说，这些业务很复杂，如果你在投资端没有搭建好合适的风险管理基础设施，同时在运营端也没有——而运营端的风险管理基础设施其实覆盖并触及公司的每一个部分，从人力资本到投资者资本，再到技术等等——

turns.en: And it's very easy for both issues on the operation side to have an impact on the investment side and vice versa. And you have a market event like Lehman, and you're really putting what's been built at a firm to that ultimate test, the amount of market volatility, the amount of price action. As you said, in this case,
turns.zh: 那么运营端的问题很容易就会影响到投资端，反之亦然。当你遇到像 Lehman 这样的市场事件时，你其实是在把一家公司一直以来搭建起来的一切放到终极考验之下——市场波动的幅度、价格波动的幅度。就像你说的，在这个案例里，

turns.en: you're dealing with Lehman as a primary brokerage counterparty where you have your assets and cash. You're dealing with them as an ISDA counterparty that all of a sudden has its unexpected default. And it was the first default of a broker dealer, I think since Drexel in 1999-91,
turns.zh: 你要面对 Lehman 作为一家主经纪商对手，你的资产和现金都放在那里。你还要面对它作为一家 ISDA 对手，突然之间发生了意料之外的违约。我想这是自 Drexel 在1999-91年以来，第一家违约的经纪交易商，

turns.en: you had that brief scare with Bear Stearns six months earlier, but that was, in essence, just to blip, obviously the government came in and arranged that quick marriage to JP Morgan. So no one really got to experience what maybe could have happened in that situation. And I think in some respect, when Lehman did actually go under,
turns.zh: 六个月前 Bear Stearns 也曾让你短暂地吓了一跳，但那本质上只是一个小插曲，显然政府介入并安排了它跟 JP Morgan 的快速联姻。所以没人真正体验到那种情形下本来可能发生什么。我想从某种意义上说，当 Lehman 真的倒下时，

turns.en: I think it was quite a shock to markets, it obviously caused huge concerns of contagion. And as a firm that's managing assets at different places and dealing with different categories, trying to figure out where the contagion could spread was really an incredible event to be a part of. And things are moving quite quickly.
turns.zh: 我觉得它给市场带来了相当大的冲击，显然引发了对连锁传染的巨大担忧。而作为一家在多个地方管理资产、跟不同类别打交道的公司，要搞清楚传染可能扩散到哪里，真的是身处其中才会体会到的极不平凡的事件。而且事情发展得非常快。

turns.en: You're having to figure out how to terminate your ISDAs with Lehman, had to figure out what traits to offset, what traits to transfer, how to manage that risk, you're scrambling to figure out across multiple jurisdictions, both in Europe and the US, how to get a hold of your assets and what risk you might be subject to
turns.zh: 你得想办法终止你跟 Lehman 的 ISDA，得搞清楚哪些交易要对冲掉、哪些交易要转移、如何管理这些风险，你要在欧洲和美国多个司法辖区之间手忙脚乱地弄清楚，怎么才能拿到你的资产，以及如果无法结算这些资产，你可能面临什么风险，

turns.en: if you can't settle those assets, you're trying to figure out unsettled trades and how your position there and what the risks were, unclear whether they were going to settle or not settle. And then for a firm that specializes in distress, you also have this enormous opportunity set of the largest distress balance sheet in history
turns.zh: 你要想办法弄清楚未结算的交易、你在其中的头寸、以及风险有多大，也不清楚它们到底会不会结算。然后，对于一家专门做困境投资的公司来说，你还面临着史上最大的困境资产负债表这样一个巨大的机会集合，

turns.en: and working to understand what the opportunities that was in your portfolio was really this dual front of both for an operational risk-matchable perspective, understanding where you stood and how to mitigate those risks. And at the same time, one of the most significant investment opportunities ever
turns.zh: 要努力去理解其中存在于你投资组合里的机会，这真的是双线作战：一方面从运营风险的角度，搞清楚你所处的位置、以及如何缓释这些风险；另一方面，这是有史以来最重大的投资机会之一，

turns.en: and to ensure that you're able to capitalize on it. And I think it did put to test firms at different philosophies in terms of what expertise they want to have in house versus outsourish. You make different decisions along that continuum at different points in your life cycle and different cost-benefit of when you want to invest capital
turns.zh: 要确保你能够抓住它。我认为它确实考验了那些在'哪些专业能力要自建、哪些要外包'上持有不同理念的公司。在生命周期的不同节点，你会沿着这条连续谱做出不同的选择，也会在'何时投入资本

turns.en: to have your own capabilities. I'd say it really was a time where having your own proprietary technology stack, having your own legal expertise really cross multiple regions and understanding the ins and outs of bankruptcy and different jurisdictions, it was showtime in a sense, right? In terms of putting everything that it had been built
turns.zh: 去自建能力'上有不同的成本收益考量。我想说，那真的是一个时刻——拥有自己的专有技术栈、拥有自己横跨多个地区的法律专业能力、理解破产程序在不同司法辖区里的种种门道，某种意义上就是'见真章的时刻'，对吧？就是把你一直以来搭建的

turns.en: to that point to the test and it was obviously a seminal event for markets it would play out for many, many years. Kingshire was fortunate to actually have positive returns in 2008. You obviously had a huge swath of the industry that was down 20, 30, sometimes more percent. You had lots of funds forced to gate. It was a very risky time.
turns.zh: 一切都放到考验之下。这显然是市场上一个具有里程碑意义的事件，它的影响会持续很多很多年。King Street 很幸运，在2008年实际上取得了正回报。而显然，行业里有一大片公司是下跌20%、30%、有时更多的。很多基金被迫设置赎回门槛（gate）。那是一段风险极高的时期。

turns.en: Things did somewhat bounce back relatively quickly in the scheme of things as you got to end of 2009, a lot at bounce back. But it was a period where certainly some firms didn't make it through that period. Certainly firms were not able to take advantage of the opportunity set because of the issues they were dealing with.
turns.zh: 从整体来看，事情确实反弹得相对较快，到了2009年底，很多东西都反弹了回来。但那也是一段时期，肯定有一些公司没能熬过去。肯定也有公司因为自身正在应对的问题，而无法抓住当时的机会集合。

turns.en: So it really was a live situation of really the importance of being thoughtful about what you're building because oftentimes you don't realize the benefits of it until you're in that so-called disaster scenario. But we talk a lot about risk management on this podcast, whether it's through diversification,
turns.zh: 所以这真是一个活生生的例子，说明在搭建东西时深思熟虑有多重要，因为往往你要等到身处那种所谓的灾难情境中，才意识到它的好处。不过我们在这个播客里经常谈风险管理，无论是通过分散化，

turns.en: through derivative strategies like buying puts insurance. And as you'd mentioned your work on behalf of ISDA, I'm curious as that financial crisis hit where there are certain decisions that you and your team had made with regard to some of the complexities whether they're in credit support annexes
turns.zh: 通过买入看跌期权（put）这类衍生策略来做保险。你也提到过你代表 ISDA 所做的工作，我很好奇，当那场金融危机袭来时，你和你的团队针对其中一些复杂性——无论是在信用支持附件（credit support annex）里，

turns.en: in subtleties around market disruption events that were some kind of form of you guys basically buying optionality or at least being very careful not to be short optionality on some of these contingent events that you didn't think would happen but ultimately did happen. Yeah, look, I'd say that we always try to take the approach
turns.zh: 还是在市场中断事件（market disruption event）周边的那些微妙之处——是否做过某种形式的决策，基本上就是你们在买入选择权（optionality），或者至少非常小心地不去做空选择权，针对某些你本以为不会发生、但最终确实发生了的或有事件。是的，瞧，我想说我们一直努力采取这样的思路，

turns.en: of building for the future, building for success. The part that I find interesting is the founder led firms as they grow have to be really thoughtful about their evolution if they wanna migrate away from the founder being the sole risk taker. If a founder wants to run a firm
turns.zh: 它看起来和感觉起来会更加机构化。不同做法各有取舍。我觉得有意思的部分是，那些创始人主导的公司随着成长，如果想从'创始人是唯一承担风险者'迁移出去，就必须对自己的演变非常深思熟虑。如果一位创始人想经营一家

turns.en: where they're the sole risk taker, that's certainly a model that exists. It may create some self-selection bias and the type of people that you're hiring, but you could run a firm that way, you could certainly be successful. turns.zh: 自己作为唯一风险承担者的公司，那当然是一种存在的模式。它可能在你所招的人的类型上产生某种自我选择偏差，但你可以那样经营一家公司，你当然也可以很成功。我觉得有意思的是，从那种模式转型出来，需要相当大的重塑。

turns.en: Again, across all parts of the firm, as you move from one decision maker to many, there's so many things that have to change and evolve, not the least of which as we talked about, is there risk management infrastructure and how you think about that? But how you lead and manage takes on a whole new element to it.
turns.zh: 同样，是公司所有部分的重组。当你从一个决策者变成许多决策者时，有太多东西必须改变和演变，其中最重要的，正如我们谈过的，是风险管理基础设施、以及你如何思考它。但你如何领导和管理，也带上了全新的一层含义。

turns.en: How you hire, how you structure incentives and your compensation arrangements, your partnership arrangements, if you're gonna have a partnership structure where you wanna have others be part of the success of the firm, that becomes quite important. Retention becomes quite important. The founder's not gonna go anywhere, absent,
turns.zh: 你如何招聘、如何设计激励和薪酬安排、你的合伙安排——如果你要有一个合伙结构，想让别人也成为公司成功的一部分——那就变得相当重要。人才留任变得相当重要。创始人是不会走的，除非

turns.en: apocryphal hit by a bus, but when you rely on other people who you're putting in senior leadership positions, they may be running a product, they may be prominent members of an investment committee. You really need to think long and hard about lining incentives. You need to think long and hard
turns.zh: 那种传说中的'被公交车撞了'。但当你依赖其他人、把他们放到高级领导岗位上时——他们可能在管理一个产品，可能是投资委员会里的重要成员——你真的需要认真思考如何对齐激励。你需要认真思考

turns.en: about how those people interface with your investor base. And you wanna create an enduring institution that involves more people, more dimensions to it. And in some ways, just a lot more moving parts than the small founder led firm. So the transitions that have to occur along the way,
turns.zh: 这些人如何跟你的投资者群体对接。而你想打造一个能长久的机构，它涉及更多的人、更多的维度。在某种意义上，它比小型的创始人主导公司有更多得多的活动部件。所以一路上必须发生的那些转变，

turns.en: I find quite interesting and challenging at the same time, because it does involve pretty significant changes by a founder in particular. So I'll throw two scenarios at you. I'd love to get your thoughts on this. So the first one would be, there's plenty of really, really intelligent investors out there, very good at generating returns,
turns.zh: 我觉得既非常有意思，同时也很有挑战，因为它确实涉及创始人一方相当大的改变。那我给你抛两个情境吧，我很想听听你的想法。第一个是，市面上有很多非常非常聪明、非常擅长创造回报的投资者，

turns.en: have done it for years, and yet maybe they're stuck at something, I don't know, $200 to $400 million. It's not really in this day and age, given the cost of running a hedge fund in the infrastructure, it's not really at scale, but they're kind of stuck. That's the first scenario. And the second scenario is kind of the opposite.
turns.zh: 做这行很多年了，但也许他们卡在某个规模上，我不知道，2亿到4亿美元之间。以如今运营一家对冲基金的成本和基础设施来看，这其实并不算有规模，但他们就是有点卡住了。这是第一个情境。第二个情境则差不多是相反的。

turns.en: Maybe this is situational awareness, which is they just got enormous, very fast. I think I read that that firm had 18 people or something with $20 billion of capital, so that they're thoroughly success from a returns and capital standpoint far exceeds their infrastructure and maybe capacity to really support that capital internally.
turns.zh: 也许这就是 Situational Awareness，也就是他们一下子就变得极其庞大、非常快。我记得我读到过，那家公司大概只有18个人，却管理着200亿美元的资本，所以他们在回报和资本上的巨大成功，远远超过了他们的基础设施、也许还有真正在内部支撑这些资本的能力。

turns.en: Take us through how you would engage with each of those. The first one being a really, really intelligent investor whose returns are great, but just can't seem to raise the kind of capital that is needed to make an ongoing enterprise. I guess in the first, it would be digging into what's driving this lack of growth.
turns.zh: 带我们看看你会如何分别应对这两种情境。第一种是一位非常非常聪明、回报很棒、但似乎就是无法募集到让公司持续经营所需资本的投资者。我想在第一种情境里，会先去深挖是什么在导致这种增长的缺失。

turns.en: All of us being equal affirms that are successful, performance-wise, tend to attract capital, all of us being equal. So it would be an examination into what's driving this lack of growth. Is the strategy to niche? Maybe there's a perception that there's not enough capacity to grow the strategy.
turns.zh: 在其他条件相同的情况下，业绩成功的公司往往会吸引资本，其他条件相同的话。所以这会是一次审视，去弄清是什么在导致这种增长的缺失。是策略太小众了吗？也许存在一种认知，觉得这个策略没有足够的容量去成长。

turns.en: Is it an issue of attracting the right investor base, which I would say in your fact pattern is probably a key factor, where either they don't have someone capable to assist in the marketing function. Perhaps the founder is now articulating the strategy well to the potential investor base. Perhaps they don't have the right team.
turns.zh: 是不是吸引合适投资者群体的问题？我会说，在你描述的这个情形里，这可能是一个关键因素，也就是他们要么没有一个有能力协助营销职能的人，也许是创始人没能把策略很好地表述给潜在的投资者群体，也许他们没有一支合适的团队。

turns.en: Is there a turnover issue that could be other issues that despite good performance is standing in the way? So it would be an examination of the historical path of the firm, what its organization looks like, what its investment process and strategy and its capacity look like, and trying to figure out which parts are falling down
turns.zh: 是不是有人员流动（turnover）的问题？也可能有其他问题，尽管业绩不错，却挡在路上。所以这会是一次审视：回顾这家公司走过的历史路径，它的组织长什么样，它的投资流程、策略和容量长什么样，并试图弄清楚哪些部分出了问题，

turns.en: and devising a strategy to address that. So if it's an investor issue, perhaps it's doing a real search for a high-level IR marketing professional that can really assist in raising capital. If it's an investment capability standpoint, maybe it's thinking through what adjacencies there might be
turns.zh: 然后制定一套应对策略。所以如果是投资者层面的问题，也许就是要认真去物色一位高水平的投资者关系（IR）、营销专业人士，真正能够协助募集资本。如果是投资能力层面的问题，也许就是要想清楚可能存在哪些相邻的延展方向（adjacency），

turns.en: and how do you attract additional senior talent to the firm to take advantage of that. Maybe it's there are new product opportunities that might attract a different investor base. So that could be part of it. So lots of things that could drive that. So we really involve a detailed analysis of the firm, its organization, the people,
turns.zh: 以及你如何吸引额外的资深人才加入公司来抓住它。也许是有新的产品机会，能够吸引一个不同的投资者群体，所以这也可能是其中一部分。能导致这种情况的因素有很多。所以这真的涉及对这家公司、它的组织、它的人、

turns.en: and all the different functions of it. Let's go to the opposite one. A firm has incredible early success, maybe sizzling returns. As you said, returns attract capital. The firm gets really way too big, capital-wise for its own infrastructure. What to do there? What's your approach and your thought process in terms of advising them?
turns.zh: 以及它所有不同职能的一次细致分析。我们来看相反的那个情境。一家公司取得了惊人的早期成功，也许回报炙手可热。正如你所说，回报吸引资本。这家公司在资本上长得实在太大，超过了自己基础设施的承载力。那该怎么办？在给他们建议时，你的思路和想法是什么？

turns.en: I don't know, facts of the situation, we're going to start with what's in the press, but that's a challenging problem from a standpoint of the growth seems to be so exponential. That you probably find it hard to believe that there's a good institutional underfooting for the operations of the business.
turns.zh: 我不知道，这要看具体情况，我们就从媒体报道里看到的东西说起，但从增长看起来如此呈指数级的角度讲，这是个很有挑战性的问题。你大概会觉得难以置信，公司业务的运营底下有扎实的机构化根基。

turns.en: And that's not something that's very easy to just snap your fingers and create. I do think firms that grow purposefully and doesn't have to be slow slow, but just methodically think tend to fare better than you oftentimes see these mega launches of hundreds of people that just start out of nowhere.
turns.zh: 而这又不是那种打个响指就能轻易创造出来的东西。我确实认为，那些有目的地成长的公司——不必很慢很慢，但要有条不紊地思考——往往会表现得更好。你经常看到这种几百人的巨型启动，凭空冒出来。

turns.en: I'm not having worked at those firms specifically. I just don't think you create the right base to create the right culture in particular. You're hiring hundreds of people into a culture that doesn't even exist yet. You're creating it as you go. You're sort of building the plane as you're flying it.
turns.zh: 我并没有专门在那些公司工作过，我只是觉得你没法打造出合适的根基，尤其是没法打造出合适的文化。你是在往一个尚不存在的文化里招几百个人。你是在一边走一边创造它，有点像一边飞一边造飞机。

turns.en: I think if you're already at that point, you probably have to think long and hard about how do you contract where you are to get to a more manageable level and then try to backfill for the resources that you might need across the different functions of the business, but I would think of it. Again, fairly methodically is my first example
turns.zh: 我想如果你已经到了那个地步，你大概就得认真思考，如何把现在的规模收缩到一个更可控的水平，然后再去回填你在业务各个职能上可能需要的资源。但我会有条不紊地去思考它。我的第一个例子，

turns.en: of it's really thinking through every function of the business and do you have the right resources, not just for the current business, but for where you want to take it. Again, that's everything from human capital management to technology, to back office, to legal compliance, to tax, et cetera.
turns.zh: 就是真正去想清楚业务的每一个职能，你有没有合适的资源，不只是为了当前的业务，也是为了你想把它带到的地方。再说一次，这涵盖从人力资本管理到技术、到后台、到法律合规、到税务等等的一切。

turns.en: In some cases, you can swap team in some external parties, some outsource providers, so in your second example, that's probably a solution in the short term of how do you just get some third party help across the different aspects that perhaps was not as built out as they could or should be. And those are also important decisions
turns.zh: 在某些情况下，你可以引入一些外部机构、一些外包服务商。所以在你的第二个例子里，这在短期内大概是一个解决方案，就是如何在那些也许没有搭建到应有程度的不同方面，弄到一些第三方的帮助。而这些也是重要的决策，

turns.en: that firms undertake at different points in their life cycle of where do they want to outsource, where do they want to insource? Those are also quite important decisions thinking through where you want to have more control or less control. Those are obviously also questions on the technology front. If you're building or buying technology,
turns.zh: 公司在生命周期的不同节点会去面对：他们想在哪里外包、想在哪里自建（insource）？这些也是相当重要的决策，要想清楚你想在哪里拥有更多或更少的控制权。这些显然也是技术层面的问题。如果你是在自建还是采购技术，

turns.en: those are common decision trees of when do you want to build versus buy? And again, note one size fits all for a given type of technology or a given type of firm, but making those decisions around what you want to have control over and have capabilities in house versus where do you want to leverage third parties?
turns.zh: 这些都是常见的决策树，就是你什么时候想自建、什么时候想买。而且再说一次，对某一类技术或某一类公司来说，并没有'一刀切'的答案，但要围绕'你想自己掌控什么、想在内部具备什么能力'，相对于'你想在哪里借助第三方'来做这些决策，

turns.en: And how do you change that calculus as you grow and evolve? I think is also important. Let's finish off with some of your thoughts on AI. So today, anthropic has said that I want to say by Thanksgiving, it wants to go public. So we're seeing a lot from these large language models. They hold great promise.
turns.zh: 以及随着你成长和演变，你如何改变这个权衡，我认为也很重要。我们最后来聊聊你对人工智能（AI）的一些想法吧。今天，Anthropic 说，我想大概是到感恩节之前，它想上市。所以我们从这些大语言模型（large language model）身上看到很多。它们蕴含着巨大的前景。

turns.en: Of course, there's these sandbox issues talking about risks of hacking and things going rogue. What do you see there in terms of the promise and also maybe the risk side for your clients? How are you incorporating AI into the process of advising them? It's remarkable what's evolved in that space in a short period of time.
turns.zh: 当然，也有这些'沙盒'（sandbox）层面的问题，谈到被黑客攻击、以及失控的风险。在这方面你怎么看，既有前景、也许还有对你客户而言的风险一面？你又是如何把 AI 融入给他们提供建议的流程中的？在这个领域里，短短一段时间内演变出的东西令人瞩目。

turns.en: It's a topic that is front of mind for every firm I'm talking to. Every firm is trying to figure out how to use it, when to use it, where to use it, what capabilities you want to have in-house, can they leverage third parties, what functions to prioritize, et cetera. And if you're a very large firm and you've
turns.zh: 这是我正在沟通的每一家公司都放在心头的头号话题。每家公司都在试图搞清楚怎么用它、什么时候用它、在哪里用它、你想在内部具备哪些能力、能不能借助第三方、优先做哪些职能等等。如果你是一家非常大的公司，而且

turns.en: got your own capabilities, that becomes an easier equation. But many firms in the asset management world are not at that state. They don't have dozens of engineers capable of really understanding the technology and the safeguards that need to be built, but more importantly, creating orchestration layers
turns.zh: 已经具备了自己的能力，那这就成了一个更容易的等式。但资产管理世界里的很多公司并不在那个状态。他们没有几十名工程师，能够真正理解这项技术、理解需要搭建哪些安全保障，但更重要的是，去围绕它创建编排层（orchestration layer）

turns.en: and frameworks around it to be able to put against their business use cases. So it is a huge need. And I've been working with a few different people that I tend to refer and partner with into my clients to help build infrastructure and use cases that are action-oriented and things that you don't spend six months in a workshop developing,
turns.zh: 和框架，以便把它对接到自己的业务用例上。所以这是一个巨大的需求。我一直在跟几个不同的人合作，我倾向于把他们引荐给我的客户、跟他们结伴，去帮助搭建基础设施，以及以行动为导向的用例，是那种你不会花六个月在研讨会里开发、

turns.en: waiting for a product, things that you can implement very, very quickly. But it's a need that every firm has. And it's pretty clear that just allowing your firm, OK, we've got client enterprise, here you go. That's not what we're talking about. I thought obviously has some benefits and can be impactful.
turns.zh: 等着一个产品的东西，而是那种你能非常非常快落地的东西。但这是每家公司都有的需求。而且很清楚的是，仅仅让你的公司，好，我们上了企业版（Enterprise），拿去用吧，这并不是我们在谈的东西。我想那显然有一些好处、也能产生影响。

turns.en: But to really harness AI, you need to really give it access to the broadest array of information, both internal and external. Obviously, there are security questions and concerns that come into play as part of that. And you want to have ability to link that information across your firm.
turns.zh: 但要真正驾驭 AI，你需要真正让它能够访问最广泛的信息，既包括内部的也包括外部的。显然，这其中会牵扯到安全方面的疑问和顾虑。而且你希望能够跨公司把这些信息串联起来。

turns.en: You want to have the ability to create, in essence, customized applications, customized dashboards to solve business problems. And to be able to do that, I think you really have to have this marrying of both technological capability with functional domain expertise. There are lots of AI consultants floating around.
turns.zh: 你希望能够创建，本质上说，定制化的应用、定制化的仪表盘来解决业务问题。而要能做到这一点，我认为你真的必须把技术能力与职能领域的专业知识结合起来。市面上有很多 AI 顾问在到处跑。

turns.en: If you're trying to put an AI consultant against an investment business and they don't understand investing, I'm just not sure that that's going to achieve the success that you want to achieve. I think if you can implement different AI use cases where you've got this marrying of domain and technical expertise
turns.zh: 如果你想让一个 AI 顾问去对接一项投资业务，而他们又不懂投资，我就是不太确定那能达成你想要的成功。我认为，如果你能落地不同的 AI 用例，把领域专业知识和技术专业知识结合起来，

turns.en: where someone understands the pitfalls of the data you're trying to connect, understands, if you're an investment professional, what are those use cases that are going to be really impactful? If that's been professional, say, hey, I want to see this. The person can textualize that because they have some real investment experience.
turns.zh: 让某人既理解你想要连接的数据的陷阱，又——如果你是一位投资专业人士——理解哪些用例才是真正有影响力的。如果是那位专业人士说，嘿，我想看这个，那么这个人就能把它情境化（contextualize），因为他有真正的投资经验。

turns.en: So I'm fine there potentially use cases, maybe without that. But I do think there's more power on the AI front when you're marrying those two things together. And it is going to dramatically change how firms look and operate. It doesn't mean you necessarily going to be able to replace lots of people immediately.
turns.zh: 所以，我觉得那里可能有一些用例，也许不需要那样也能做。但我确实认为，当你把这两样东西结合起来时，AI 这一面会更有力量。而且它将极大地改变公司的样貌和运营方式。这不意味着你一定能马上替换掉很多人。

turns.en: But I think it will change the face of how a firm looks. I think it will certainly impact the technology footprint that firms employ. I think it will impact the way they think about information. And I think, again, people are trying to figure it out. But there's also this interesting aspect of firms that think about
turns.zh: 但我认为它会改变一家公司的样貌。我认为它肯定会影响到公司所采用的技术布局。我认为它会影响他们思考信息的方式。而且我认为，再说一次，人们都在试图搞清楚它。但这里还有一个有意思的方面，就是那些公司在思考

turns.en: taking AI and applying it to traditional processes and how do you overlay it versus where do you just need to redesign the entire process to be from the AI point of view, as opposed to trying to put an AI process on top of an existing process that's not really created with AI in mind.
turns.zh: 把 AI 拿来应用到传统流程上时，你是如何把它叠加上去，相对于你在哪里干脆就需要从 AI 的角度重新设计整个流程，而不是试图把一个 AI 流程套在一个当初并不是以 AI 为念去创建的现有流程之上。

turns.en: Where does it just need to be entirely rebuilt from the ground up? So I think there's some interesting aspects there that I don't think we know yet how it's going to play out. But it is an incredibly impactful technology that every firm needs to think through what are the highest priorities, how are they going to leverage it?
turns.zh: 哪里干脆就需要从头到尾彻底重建？所以我认为这里面有一些有意思的方面，我觉得我们还不知道它会如何演变。但它是一项极具影响力的技术，每家公司都需要想清楚，哪些是最高优先级、他们要如何利用它、

turns.en: What kind of financial investment do they want to make? This can obviously be quite expensive. Certainly aspects of it can be fun expenses, but thinking through the magnitude of that, I think is important. And these things are evolving so quickly that thinking through what infrastructure you're tying yourself to
turns.zh: 他们想做多大的财务投入？这显然可能相当昂贵。当然其中某些方面可以是运营开支（operating expense），但想清楚那个投入的量级，我认为很重要。而且这些东西演变得太快了，所以想清楚你把自己绑定在了什么样的基础设施上、

turns.en: and how easily can or can't you switch, I think, is going to be interesting.
